passages.name: Listen & Speak 1 ①
passages.flow: 환영 인사 → 감사 + 기대 → 환영한 이유 → 약속하며 마무리
lines: Hey, Bora. Welcome to our rock band.
Thanks. I’m looking forward to playing in a concert with you.
We’re excited to have a new guitar player.
Great. See you on Friday.
cues: 첫 문장: 이름을 부르며 밴드에 온 걸 환영
새 기타 연주자(= Bora)가 와서 신난다 — 환영하는 쪽의 말

passages.name: Listen & Speak 1 ②
passages.flow: 뭐 읽어? → 책 소개 → 인물 확인 → 보충 → 영화 얘기 → 제목? → 답 → 같이 가자 → 약속
lines: Jiho, what are you reading?
I’m reading a book about a baseball player named Jim Abbott.
Oh, the man who was born without a right hand?
That’s right. He tried really hard and even won the MVP award.
Yeah. His story was made into a movie. I’m going to watch it this Saturday.
Really? What’s the title?
Our Hero. I’m really looking forward to watching it.
Can I join you?
Sure. See you on Saturday.
cues: 첫 문장: 이름 부르며 뭐 읽는지 질문
'That's right' = 바로 앞 확인 질문에 긍정 + 보충
'His story' = Jim Abbott 이야기 → 영화 얘기로 전환
'같이 봐도 돼?' — 토요일에 본다는 말을 들은 뒤

passages.name: Listen & Speak 2 ①
passages.flow: 숙제 끝냈어? → 아직, 어려워 → 맞아, 재밌기도 해 → 그럼 도와줄래? → 거절 + 이유
lines: Minho, did you finish the math homework?
Not yet. Math is difficult.
Yes, but it’s interesting, too.
Then can you help me with my math homework?
I’d love to, but I can’t. I have to take care of my brother.

passages.name: Listen & Speak 2 ②
passages.flow: 대회 참가 소식 → 축하 → 기타 칠 줄 알지? → 응 → 반주 부탁 → 거절 + 이유 → 유감 → 응원 약속
lines: Alex, I’m going to take part in a singing contest next Monday.
That’s great, Sumin!
You know how to play the guitar, right?
Yes, I’ve played the guitar for 3 years.
Great. Can you play the guitar while I sing in the contest?
I’d love to, but I can’t. I hurt my hand in gym class yesterday.
Oh! I’m sorry to hear that.
Thanks. But I’ll be there to cheer for you.
cues: 첫 문장: 노래 대회 참가 소식

passages.name: Real Life Talk
passages.flow: 주말 계획? → 뮤지컬 → 무슨 내용? → 소개 → 주연? → 답 → 좋아하는 배우 → 같이 갈래? → 거절 + 이유 → 다음에
lines: Hi, Tony! What are you going to do this weekend?
I’m going to watch the musical, Billy Elliot.
Billy Elliot? What is it about?
It’s about a boy who became a famous dancer. I’m looking forward to watching it.
Sounds interesting. Who is the main actor?
Jason Kim. He’s a great dancer.
He’s my favorite actor. I watched his musical last year.
Oh, really? Do you want to join me?
I’d love to, but I can’t. I have volunteer work this weekend.
Okay. Maybe next time!
cues: 첫 문장: 인사 + 주말 계획 질문

passages.name: 본문 1
passages.flow: 기쁨의 눈물 → 감정 → 비유 → 둘러봄 → 단원들 → 상황 설명(연주회 끝) → 감회 → 긴 여정
lines: Tears of joy are rolling down my cheeks.
I’m so happy and thrilled.
If I were a bird, I would fly.
I look around.
The other members in my orchestra are hugging one another.
Our concert has just finished and everyone is standing and giving us a big hand.
None of us ever expected that this day would come.
It has been a long journey.
cues: 첫 문장: 눈물 흘리는 장면으로 시작
왜 이런 상황인지 설명: 연주회가 막 끝남
긴 여정이었다는 마무리 → 다음 글(과거 이야기)로 연결

passages.name: 본문 2
passages.flow: 자기소개 → 이름 질문 → 이유 → 별명 → 마을 소개 → 매립지 → 마을 자체가 매립지 → 가난 → 희망 없음 → 전환(Favio)
lines: My name is Andrea and I’m a violinist in the Recycled Orchestra.
Why is it called the Recycled Orchestra?
It’s because our musical instruments are made of objects from a landfill.
That’s why it’s also known as the Landfill Harmonic Orchestra.
Most of us in the orchestra are from Cateura, a small town in Paraguay.
There is a huge landfill in our town.
Some people even say that Cateura itself is a giant landfill.
Many of us are poor.
There weren’t many hopes and dreams in our town.
Everything began to change, however, when we met Favio Chávez.
cues: 'it' = 방금 말한 오케스트라, 이름의 이유 묻기
'even' = 매립지 얘기를 한 단계 더 강조

passages.name: 본문 3
passages.flow: Favio 소개 → 가르치고 싶지만 문제 → 악기 부족 → 살 돈 없음 → 포기 안 함 → 아이디어 → Nicholas 실행 → 바이올린 → 플루트
lines: Favio was an environmental educator and a musician.
He wanted to teach us music, but there was a big problem.
There were only a few musical instruments in the whole town.
We couldn’t afford to buy new ones.
But Favio didn’t give up.
He said that we could make musical instruments with objects from the landfill.
A talented man named Nicholas was able to put this idea into practice.
He made violins from oil drums.
He turned water pipes into flutes.
cues: 첫 문장: 앞 글 끝에 나온 Favio 소개
그 문제가 뭔지: 악기가 거의 없음
'new ones' = 새 악기, 살 형편도 안 됨
'this idea' = 앞 문장의 아이디어 → 실행한 사람

passages.name: 본문 4
passages.flow: 또 다른 문제 → 연주 못함 → 악보도 못 읽음 → Favio의 인내 → 소리 내기 시작 → 첫 곡 회상 → 짧고 음 안 맞음 → 그래도 아름다움 → 새 희망 → 매일 연습 → 어느 날 소식 → 진짜 공연 → 현재(수백 명 앞) → 사랑받음 → 마지막 문장
lines: We had another problem.
No one knew how to play musical instruments.
We didn’t even know how to read music.
Favio taught us with great patience.
Step by step, we began to make some sounds on our instruments.
I still remember the first piece of music that we played.
It was very short and mostly out of tune.
But it was the most beautiful music to us.
We felt a new hope in our hearts.
From then on, we gathered to practice every day.
One day, Favio told us some great news.
We were going to have a concert, a real concert!
And here we are now in front of hundreds of people.
They love our music.
The world sends us trash, but we send back music!
cues: 첫 문장: 'another problem' = 악기 문제 다음의 또 다른 문제
가르침의 결과: 조금씩 소리 내기 시작
'here we are now' = 현재(연주회 끝난 장면)로 복귀

passages.name: Listen & Speak 1 ①
passages.flow: 초대 감사 → 와 줘서 기쁨 → 꽃 선물 → 감사
lines: Hi, Lisa. Thank you for inviting me to your birthday party.
My pleasure. I’m glad you could come.
These flowers are for you. Happy birthday!
They are beautiful! Thank you.
cues: 첫 문장: 인사 + 초대해 줘서 고맙다

passages.name: Listen & Speak 1 ②
passages.flow: 기차 곧 떠남 → 여행 즐거웠길 → 물론 → 어디가 제일? → 민속촌 → 인기 장소 → 한복 → 기쁨 → 구경 감사 → 천만에·잘 가
lines: Sumin, my train is leaving in five minutes.
I hope you enjoyed your trip, Daniel.
Of course, I did.
Which place did you like most in my town?
I liked the folk village most.
Yeah, it’s the most popular place here.
I really liked walking around in hanbok. I looked really cool.
I’m glad to hear that.
Thank you for showing me around.
It was my pleasure. Have a safe trip.
cues: 떠나는 Daniel에게 여행 소감 묻는 말
'I did' = enjoyed, 바로 앞 말에 대한 답
감사에 답 + 잘 가라는 작별 인사

passages.name: Listen & Speak 2 ①
passages.flow: 우산 반입 금지 → 어디에 둬? → 우산꽂이 → 알겠다·감사
lines: Excuse me. You’re not allowed to bring your umbrella inside.
Oh, where should I put it?
There is an umbrella stand outside.
Okay. I’ll put it there. Thank you.

passages.name: Listen & Speak 2 ②
passages.flow: 표 판매 중 → 예매하자 → 11월 5일 남음 → 학생표 2장 → 동생 데려가도? → 되지만 8세 미만 금지 → 10살 → 어린이표 추가·총액 → 좋아 → 기대
lines: The tickets for the World Music Concert are on sale now.
Really? Let’s book the tickets online right away.
Okay. Let’s see.... There are still tickets left for November 5th.
Sounds good. Let’s get two student tickets.
Oh, do you mind if I bring my little brother?
Not at all. But it says that you are not allowed to bring children under 8.
No problem. He’s 10.
Okay, I’ll add one child ticket. The total price is 25 dollars.
Great.
I can’t wait to see the concert!
cues: 'Not at all' = 괜찮다 + 조건(8세 미만 금지)

passages.name: Real Life Talk
passages.flow: 환영 인사 → 개관 연도 → 그 이후 전시 → 오늘 볼 것 → 규칙 예고 → 규칙 내용 → 시작
lines: Hello, students! Thank you for visiting our art museum.
This museum opened in 1995.
Since then, it has exhibited many famous artworks.
Today, you will see some famous artworks from the art books.
Before we begin the tour, let me remind you of a basic rule.
You can take pictures of the artworks, but you’re not allowed to touch them.
Now let’s start the tour.

passages.name: 본문 1
passages.flow: 표현 질문 → 예술가는 자연에서 영감 → 이유(자연이 아름다움) → 형태가 보기 좋음 → 예: 달걀 → 아름답지 않나 → 달걀의 특징 → 달걀 모양 건물? → 런던에 실제 존재
lines: Have you heard of the expression, “Art imitates nature”?
Many artists get their ideas and inspirations from the world around them.
This is because the natural world is a beautiful place.
The shapes in nature are very pleasing to the eye.
For example, look at the egg on the left.
Isn’t it beautiful?
It is round and delicate, yet strong enough to protect its contents.
Can you imagine a building that looks like an egg?
Such a building actually exists in London.
cues: 첫 문장: 표현을 들어 봤냐는 질문으로 시작
그 표현의 뜻 풀이(예술가는 주변 세상에서 영감)
'This is because' = 왜 자연에서 얻는지 이유
'Such a building' = 달걀 모양 건물, 실제 존재

passages.name: 본문 2
passages.flow: 자연이 건축가에게 영감 → 사그라다 파밀리아 → 유명한 성당 → 기둥을 봐라 → 나무 같지? → 가우디가 나무 형태 사용 → 그렇게 자연을 실내로
lines: Nature has inspired many architects around the world.
This is the Sagrada Familia in Spain.
It is one of the most famous churches in the world.
Look at the beautiful tall columns inside the church.
They look like trees, don’t they?
The famous architect, Antoni Gaudi, used the shape of trees in the Sagrada Familia.
That’s how he brought the beauty of nature indoors.
cues: 첫 문장: 이 글의 주제(건축가 + 자연)
'the church' = 그 성당 → 안의 기둥 보라
나무처럼 보이는 이유 = 가우디가 나무 형태 사용

passages.name: 본문 3
passages.flow: 앞 두 예시는 쉽게 보임 → 호주 예시는 안 그럼 → 웃손: 자연 형태 + 상상력 → 뭐에서 영감? → 파도·돛단배 추측 → 사실은 오렌지 → 지붕 자세히 → 껍질 보여? → 조명 켜면 더 잘 보임
lines: In the first two examples, we can easily see what inspired the architect.
But in the next example from Australia, this is not so obvious.
Jørn Utzon, the architect of the Sydney Opera House, took a shape from nature and added his imagination.
Can you guess what inspired him?
Many people think that it is the waves in the ocean or a sailing boat.
But interestingly, the inspiration came from an orange.
Look at the roof closely.
Can you see the peels of an orange?
When orange lights are shone on the building, you can see the peels more clearly.
cues: 첫 문장: 앞의 두 예시(달걀·나무) 정리
호주 예시 = 시드니 오페라 하우스 소개
'more clearly' = 껍질이 더 잘 보이는 조건

passages.name: 본문 4
passages.flow: 한국은? → DDP 가 봤어? → 우주선 같다 생각 → 하지만 자연의 곡선 → 덕분에 관광 명소 → 보다시피 많은 건물이 자연을 담음 → 완벽한 예 → 너라면?
lines: What about Korea?
Have you ever been to Dongdaemun Design Plaza in Seoul?
Many people think that the building looks like a giant spaceship.
But the architect, Zaha Hadid, took the curved lines from nature so that city people could enjoy them.
Thanks to its special design, it has become a popular tourist attraction in Seoul.
As you can see, many buildings try to capture the beauty of nature in their design.
They are perfect examples of “Nature meets city.”
If you were an architect, what would you choose from nature?
cues: 첫 문장: 외국 예시 → 한국으로 화제 전환
'its special design' = 그 곡선 디자인 → 결과(명소)
'As you can see' = 예시 전체 정리

passages.name: Listen & Speak 1 ①
passages.flow: 정상 거의 다 왔다 → 얼마나 높을까 → 약 2,000m → 와 높다 → 응, 계속 가자
lines: We’re almost at the top of the mountain.
I wonder how high this mountain is.
It’s about 2,000m high.
Wow! This is a really high mountain.
Yes, it is. Let’s keep going.
cues: 'Yes, it is' = 높다는 말에 동의 + 계속 가자

passages.name: Listen & Speak 1 ②
passages.flow: TV 펭귄 귀엽다 → 근데 추워 보임 → 남극이 제일 춥지 → 얼마나 추울까 → 7월 -58℃, 12월 -26℃ → 7월이 더 춥네 → 춥지만 눈은 적음 → 그것도 흥미롭다
lines: Look at the baby penguins on TV. They’re so cute.
Yes, but they look very cold out there.
Yeah, the South Pole is the coldest place on Earth.
I wonder how cold it is there.
The average temperature is about -58℃ in July and -26℃ in December.
Oh, then, July is colder than December there. Interesting!
Yes. Although it’s very cold there, it doesn’t snow much.
That’s interesting, too!
cues: 추워 보이는 이유 = 남극은 가장 추운 곳
'then' = 기온 듣고 내린 결론(7월이 더 춥다)

passages.name: Listen & Speak 2 ①
passages.flow: 날씨 좋다 → 소풍 어때? → 좋아, 날씨 확인해 줄래? → 오후에 비 온대 → 다음에 가자
lines: The weather is so nice outside.
Yeah. How about going on a picnic this afternoon?
Good idea. Can you check the weather?
Oh, no! The weather forecast says it’ll be rainy in the afternoon.
Let’s go another time, then.

passages.name: Listen & Speak 2 ②
passages.flow: 일요일에 뭐 해? → 등산, 같이 갈래? → 좋아, 어디? → 남산 → 경치 좋지 → 단풍 들었대 → 제일 짧은 코스 얼마나? → 약 2시간 → 일요일에 봐
lines: Sumin, what are you going to do on Sunday?
I’m going to go hiking. Do you want to join me?
I’d love to. Where do you want to go?
I’m thinking of going to Namsan.
Oh, the scenery there is so beautiful this time of year.
Right. I heard that it’s covered with red autumn leaves now.
Great. How long does the shortest hiking course take?
The Internet says it takes about two hours.
Okay, see you on Sunday!

passages.name: Real Life Talk
passages.flow: 사진 봐 → 낙타가 줄지어 → 사막 덥고 건조해 보임 → 물 없이 얼마나? → 인터넷에서 찾자 → 2주 정도 → 굉장하다 → 언젠가 같이 여행하고 싶다
lines: Check out this picture!
Wow! The camels are walking in a line in the desert.
Yeah. The desert looks very hot and dry.
I wonder how long camels can go without water in the desert.
Let’s find out on the Internet.
Okay. The Internet says they can go about two weeks without water.
Wow, that’s amazing! Camels are really interesting animals.
I want to travel with them in the desert someday.
cues: 사막 → 낙타가 물 없이 얼마나 버티는지 궁금

passages.name: 본문 1 · Sweet Dreams
passages.flow: 지구 2/3가 바다 → 신기한 것·수많은 종 → 매일 새로 배움 → 바다 동물 알아보자 → 고래들이 뭐 하는 중? → 서 있는 듯 → 사실은 자는 중 → 꼬리로 서서 잠 → 수면 근처 → 숨 쉬러 올라옴 → 완전히 안 잠듦 → 깨면 숨 쉬고 다시 잠수
lines: Two-thirds of our planet is covered by oceans.
They are full of wonder and are home to millions of species.
Every day, we are learning new things about them.
Let’s find out about some interesting sea animals.
Can you guess what these whales are doing in the picture?
It looks like they are standing up in a group.
But they are actually sleeping!
Humpback whales stand on their tails while they sleep.
They sleep near the surface.
Since they are not fish, they need to come up to breathe.
Also, they don’t fall asleep completely.
When they wake up, they come out of the water for a deep breath and dive back into the sea.
cues: 첫 문장: 지구와 바다로 크게 시작
첫 동물: 사진 속 고래 질문

passages.name: 본문 2 · Enjoy Your Meal
passages.flow: 물고기가 안 똑똑하다 생각하면 tuskfish 봐라 → 조개 열려고 도구 사용 → 조개는 모래 속에 숨음 → 입김 불어 조개 찾음 → 조개가 닫혀 못 먹음 → 포기 안 함 → 바위에 내리침 → 결국 열림
lines: If you think fish are not smart, take a look at the tuskfish.
This small fish whose favorite food is clams uses a tool to open them.
Clams usually hide under the sand, so they cannot be easily discovered.
The tuskfish blows on the sand until a clam appears.
The clam is closed tightly, so the fish cannot eat it.
But the tuskfish doesn’t give up.
It smashes the clam against a rock.
In the end, the clam opens and dinner is served.

passages.name: 본문 3 · One, Two, Three, Jump!
passages.flow: 새가 물고기 잡는 건 봤을 것 → 물고기가 새 잡는 건? → giant trevally 조심 → 170cm 80kg → 크기에 속지 마 → 빠르고 똑똑 → 새 발견·속도·거리 계산 → 뛰어올라 잡음
lines: You have probably seen a bird fly down to the sea to catch a fish.
But have you ever seen a fish jump out of the water to catch a bird?
Well, birds have to be careful when a giant trevally is around.
This fish can grow up to 170cm and 80kg.
But don’t let its size fool you.
This fish is quick and smart.
It can spot a flying bird and calculate its speed and distance.
When the bird flies nearby, the giant trevally jumps out of the water and catches it.
cues: 첫 문장: 흔히 보는 장면(새가 물고기 잡음)
'the bird' = 계산한 그 새 → 사냥 장면으로 마무리
